name: AL-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a PVI of R+15
Incumbent Dale Strong running for reelection with a large cash advantage
No public general-election polling and no expert ratings of the race
Prediction markets price the Democrat at roughly 3%
model.rationale: This is a deeply Republican northern Alabama seat where incumbent Dale Strong holds a large fundraising and cash-on-hand edge over Andrew Sneed, and prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 3% chance. With no polls or expert ratings to suggest otherwise, the fundamentals point firmly to Strong.
model.watch: Any credible general-election polling showing Sneed within single digits, or a major outside-spending surge on his behalf, would be the first sign this race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dale Strong seeks a second term representing this heavily Republican northern Alabama district, which leans about fifteen points toward the GOP at the presidential level. He enters the general election with a clear financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.5 million and holding about $1.4 million on hand, more than double the cash of Democratic challenger Andrew Sneed.

Sneed has raised a respectable sum for a challenger in this kind of district, but there are no public polls, no expert ratings, and no reported outside spending to suggest the race is competitive. Prediction markets price Strong's chances at about 95%. The seat remains firmly in Republican hands barring an unexpected shift.
